assessments.note: after fix (ppm-146/1, u10): The card's answer A is right: the KU handbook of Modern Uyghur says awu (for things considerably distant) is often said with a lengthened high intonation on the first vowel, 'aaaa(wu) terepte', with a raise of the chin. The fact asked another question (what decides the demonstrative), and the printed wording was its only one, so it was corrected in place; the body's 'shu = near the listener' was also corrected. Only one independent source describes it (no other found).
